files.rationale: Describe each level by which of the four rubric components (development, relevance to the argument, reasons, examples) are observably present and how strong they are.
Anchor the levels on the support given for the argument (reasons and examples), with relevance and development as secondary cues; each level is written to contrast with its neighbours.
Describe the levels by the proportion of the essay's body paragraphs that are relevant, explained and exemplified, using observable wording such as none, few, half, most and all.
Single score whose nine levels describe observable content situations (development, relevance, reasons, examples), one outcome per level.
Coarse-to-fine hierarchy; a choice over three bands (does not meet / partly meets / meets), then a finer choice inside each band.
Branch noul on reaching the midpoint, then separate ordered scores for the lower half and the upper half.
